persona.name: Hiroshi Kanemoto

occupation.title: Information Systems Section Chief (Joho Seisaku Kacho)
occupation.organization: DX Promotion Office of a mid-sized city hall in Fukuoka Prefecture (about 1,800 employees)
occupation.description: Owns the city's internal IT security policy and vets every SaaS request that any department files. Spends his weeks in vendor screenings, security checklists, and explaining to department heads why the tool they saw on TV cannot touch resident data. He is the gate every AI tool must pass, and he reads the data-handling appendix first.

persona.education: Law degree from Kyushu University; passed the local civil service exam at 22; later earned the Information Security Management certification (SG) and a string of IPA qualifications.
long_term_goals: Get the city through its system standardization deadline without an incident
Build a security review process that survives his transfer
See his daughter through her university entrance exams
Retire without ever appearing in a data-breach press conference
persona.style: Polite, precise, and relentlessly procedural — he answers questions with numbered conditions rather than yes or no. Writes long, carefully hedged emails and expects the same in return. In person he is warmer than his reputation, with a dry streak of humor that only appears after the second beer at section drinking parties.

traits: Detail-obsessed reader of terms of service
Fair once his conditions are met
Prone to overwork during audit season

interests: Government security guidelines (ISMAP, the LGWAN three-layer model)
Where AI meeting tools store and train on audio data
likes: Vendors who bring a completed security checklist unprompted
Domestic data centers with clear residency guarantees
dislikes: Free trials employees start without asking
Shadow IT discovered after the fact
Being framed as the person who blocks progress

beliefs: One data incident erases ten years of DX progress
Convenience is real, but accountability is legal
Every tool is safe until you read how it handles deletion requests
skills: Translating technical risk into mayor-friendly language

general: Maintains a spreadsheet of every SaaS request with rejection reasons
Attends one security seminar a month, usually online
Personally tests approved tools before rollout
Keeps a paper notebook for anything involving personnel matters

morning: 6:30 wake, checks JPCERT advisories with coffee
Drives to city hall listening to a news podcast
workday: Mornings: security reviews and vendor meetings
Afternoons: internal consultations, incident drills, policy drafting
evening: Home by 20:00 in normal months, later during audits
Shogi app or espresso tinkering after dinner
weekend: Sunday morning jog along the Chikugo River, most weeks

health.physical: Mild lower back pain from desk work; annual checkup otherwise unremarkable.
health.mental: Carries chronic low-grade vigilance; sleeps badly the week before security audits.

relationships.name: Miki Kanemoto
relationships.description: Pharmacist at a local chain; the one person he thinks aloud with about work stress, in vague terms.

relationships.name: Ono-shunin
relationships.description: A 29-year-old on his team who keeps bringing him AI tool proposals; Kanemoto rejects most but quietly respects the persistence.
